profile.headline: Employee at NVIDIA
profile.geoLocationName: Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States

positions.title: Senior Architect, GPU Compute Architecture Group
positions.description:
In the GPU Compute Architecture group, my main responsibility was the design and implementation of PTX (the Parallel Thread Execution Language), which serves as a virtual instruction set architecture and provides a stable, machine-independent compiler target for GPU Computing languages such as CUDA and OpenCL. In this role, I worked closely with a global compiler team with members in Santa Clara, California; Pune, India; and Austin, Texas. I authored PTX ISA versions 1.0 through 3.1, which shipped with CUDA versions 1.0 through 5.0.

I also contributed to our next-generation GPU architectures, working on designs for predicated execution, branch architecture, extended-precision integer instructions, and video instructions. Before joining the GPU Compute Architecture group, I wrote simulators and compiler tools for NVIDIA’s embedded video processors.

positions.title: Program Director, Efficeon TM9000 Processor
positions.description:
As director of the Efficeon TM9000 “Astro 3” processor program, my primary responsibilities were to plan and coordinate the development of Transmeta’s next-generation processor. In the early design phase, I worked with Marketing and Engineering to define the program, create a plan of record that satisfied marketing requirements, and develop and maintain the overall program schedule of milestones and deliverables. In the development phase, I coordinated activities between VLSI, Software, Systems Engineering, and Product Engineering; I held quarterly program reviews for the executive staff; and I also worked with other program managers to coordinate schedules and resource sharing between programs. I have also worked with Quality and the ISO team to define processes for each phase of the program, and I participated in ISO audits leading to successful certification.

During this period, I also acted as Project Manager for development of the Code Morphing Software (CMS) that would run on Astro 3.

positions.title: Director of Strategic Projects
positions.description: As director of the Strategic Projects group, I was responsible for initiating and leading advanced development projects related to future business opportunities. In this role, I interacted regularly with Marketing, Engineering, and the Executive Staff to coordinate our efforts and focus on near-term advanced development projects. In addition to managing the team, I presented our portfolio of projects to the CEO each quarter, met with potential corporate partners and customers, assisted with engineering due diligence of new projects and partnerships, helped triage and prioritize Transmeta patent applications, and provided input for corporate planning and strategy.

positions.title: Manager, Code Morphing Software Products
positions.description: In this role, I formed a new team to continue development and sustaining engineering of the entire code morphing software system, including interpretation, translation, optimization, runtime support, I/O, power management, upgrades, and memory management. Our small team improved performance and power efficiency of the product through two major releases and responded to OEM requests for new features and enhancements. I worked closely with Marketing, Sales, Application Engineering, and Quality to develop and deliver reliable products on time.

positions.title: Researcher, PICO Project
positions.description: The PICO Project (“Program In, Chip Out”) research focused on the vision of custom, application specific processor design. My main contribution to PICO was the development of a prototype software infrastructure for automated search-space traversal, comprising software to enable parallel search using a farm of networked workstations, storage of results in a simple database, a graphical user interface for controlling the system and browsing the resulting designs. The infrastructure was written in C++, Perl, and Tcl/Tk. On the research side, I designed and implemented algorithms for automatic generation of instruction formats for custom VLIWs. These instruction formats could be generated from a machine description of the processor’s microarchitecture and datapath.

positions.title: Researcher, Compiler and Architecture Research Group
positions.description: As a member of Bob Rau’s Compiler and Architecture Research Group, I focused my research on analysis and optimization of predicated code. I developed the first complete, accurate, and efficient dataflow analysis framework for predicated code. I was also heavily involved in the development of Elcor, our research compiler. Elcor was written in C++ and used to validate our region-based approach to VLIW compilation. Elcor was later combined with software from Wen-mei Hwu’s group at Urbana-Champaign and from Krishna Palem’s group at NYU to form the Trimaran infrastructure for research in instruction-level parallelism.

patents.title: Predicted instruction execution in parallel processors with reduced per-thread state information including choosing a minimum or maximum of two operands based on a predicate value
patents.description: A mechanism for predicated execution of instructions within a parallel processor executing multiple threads or data lanes is disclosed. Each thread or data lane executing within the parallel processor is associated with a predicate register that stores a set of 1-bit predicates. Each of these predicates can be set using different types of predicate-setting instructions, where each predicate setting instruction specifies one or more source operands, at least one operation to be performed on the source operands, and one or more destination predicates for storing the result of the operation. An instruction can be guarded by a predicate that may influence whether the instruction is executed for a particular thread or data lane or how the instruction is executed for a particular thread or data lane.

patents.title: Execution of divergent threads using a convergence barrier
patents.description: A method, system, and computer program product for executing divergent threads using a convergence barrier are disclosed. A first instruction in a program is executed by a plurality of threads, where the first instruction, when executed by a particular thread, indicates to a scheduler unit that the thread participates in a convergence barrier. A first path through the program is executed by a first divergent portion of the participating threads and a second path through the program is executed by a second divergent portion of the participating threads. The first divergent portion of the participating threads executes a second instruction in the program and transitions to a blocked state at the convergence barrier. The scheduler unit determines that all of the participating threads are synchronized at the convergence barrier and the convergence barrier is cleared.
